SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #11
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.

2. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Removing all vegetation

3. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.

5. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Tertiary consumers

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.

8. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

9. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 100 °C

10. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

11. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.

13. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

14. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture of two liquids
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

15. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. Heating until a solid melts

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Change of State? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Change of State.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Change of State.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Change of State.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Change of State.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Change of State and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Composition of Air and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
